ns2:section.sectionText: This course will meet in 343L Wohlers Hall. Entrepreneurship and innovation are important drivers of economic and social progress. In this course we will examine the individual, organizational, and institutional precursors and consequences of entrepreneurship and innovation. Relevant patterns in both developed and emerging economies will be explored. We will read broadly, drawing on foundational works, as well as more recent work. In addition, course participants will gain experience designing potential studies and practice hand collecting primary and secondary source data. This course is part of a two course sequence (Entrepreneurship & Innovation I and II)
